summary.intent: Use the GSD manager command center to discuss, plan, and execute three gap-closure phases (42: API unpin integrity, 43: FUSE write durability, 44: IPNS conflict handling) discovered during a UAT audit of the CipherBox v1.1 milestone.
summary.outcome: Phases 42 and 43 were fully completed through the entire GSD pipeline (discuss → plan → execute → code-review → verify → close); phase 44 was discussed and its CONTEXT.md committed, with planning/execution pending.

repo: The unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) was guarded only by JwtAuthGuard with no ownership check — any authenticated user could unpin any CID, enabling cross-tenant data destruction since Kubo's swarm port 4001 is publicly reachable and broadcasts provider records for all pinned CIDs via the DHT

Kubo runs with the 'server' profile in staging (docker/docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72) which only disables local-network discovery — full public DHT participation is retained, making all pinned CIDs discoverable by crawlers

Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without unpinning (shared-write.ts:450), meaning no legitimate cross-user unpin path exists — the guardedUnpin 403 oracle risk was real: uniform 2XX was chosen to avoid existence oracle leakage
The gsd commit helper (`gsd_run query commit`) returns `committed: false` as a false negative even when the commit lands — always verify with `git log`, never blind-retry the commit

pnpm flag forwarding gotcha: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test -- --testPathPattern=X` inserts an extra `--` that makes jest treat the pattern as a positional arg — use `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api exec jest --testPathPattern='X'` instead

WinFsp cross-compilation from macOS fails in `windows-future` and `winfsp-sys` registry crates — use `cargo check` to validate Windows code changes rather than attempting a full `--features winfsp` build on macOS

The repo had no .prettierignore, causing prettier to mangle markdown tables in .planning/ docs (broke regex pipes in VALIDATION.md table cells into spurious table columns) and GSD-controlled JS/MD files

1Password SSH commit signing requires `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on git Bash calls; signing failures require restarting the 1Password desktop app — NEVER use --no-verify or --no-gpg-sign as a workaround since PRs enforce signatures
Phase-specific git branches (feat/api-unpin-integrity, feat/fuse-write-durability, feat/ipns-conflict-handling) are managed automatically by GSD tooling; main stays untouched throughout

The worktree cleanup helper (`worktree.cleanup-wave`) is not idempotent — already-merged entries report `branch_mismatch` on rerun; write a reduced manifest containing only remaining entries to re-run after partial failures
Running the cleanup helper with cwd inside an agent worktree causes false `base_mismatch` errors because the helper resolves repoRoot from cwd — must always run from the canonical repo root

code.finding: Upload-compensation path fires a global pin/rm — now rerouted through guardedUnpin with D-13 race window comment documenting the known compensation race

New guardedUnpin method: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid)) → transactional row-delete + refcount → pending_unpins outbox insert if last reference → Kubo pin/rm post-commit best-effort; cross-user attempts increment audit metric and return silent 2XX

handle_release ordering enforced: journal.put(844) → handle.cleanup(892) → reply.ok(894) → spawn(904) → journal.remove-on-success(943); reply.error(libc::EIO) added to prepare_result Err arm so OS is never acked after journal fsync failure
handle_mkdir: journal.put at line 534 inside closure before reply.entry at 655; conflict arm sends FsEvent::MkdirConflict instead of warn-only; journal entry cleared only on parent-publish success

Full rewrite: JournalOp enum, JournalEntryStatus, WriteQueue with put/remove/load_all_for_vault/update_status/record_failure/ordered_for_replay; fsync barrier before OS ack is the core durability guarantee

UploadSpawnParams types corrected (ApiClient, Handle, PublishCoordinator); journal entry carried into spawn for record_failure; removal of journal entry gated on per-file IPNS publish success (mirrors Linux CR-08 fix)

BullMQ WorkerHost: drainPendingUnpins calls provider (not raw Kubo), error-isolates per row, publishes gauge; runDriftReport reads NDJSON pin ls output read-only with zero .delete( calls — detect-only by design

Kubo v0.40 with server profile and swarm port 4001 publicly exposed (tcp+udp) — server profile only disables local-network discovery, full public DHT participation retained, meaning all pinned CIDs are broadcast as provider records

workflow: GSD wave-based worktree execution: independent plans run in isolated git worktrees in parallel; worktree manifest JSON files track active agents; cleanup-wave merges back via octopus merge after all agents in a wave complete
Post-merge gates must target specific test patterns rather than full suites to avoid OOM — `pnpm exec jest --testPathPattern='vault|delete|metrics'` pattern keeps RAM bounded

Code review (gsd-code-reviewer agent) is advisory-only and must never block phase close-out; gaps found during verification spawn additional gap-closure plan waves (wave N+1) rather than failing the phase

The decision coverage gate uses literal string matching for decision IDs (e.g. `D-07:`) — plans must include explicit citation strings in must_haves sections or the gate fails mechanically even if the decision is addressed in prose
Worktree node_modules and .husky/_ untracked dirs block cleanup-wave merge — executor prompts should include explicit CLEANUP instruction to remove them before committing SUMMARY.md
When a merge leaves MERGE_HEAD (all conflicts auto-resolved but commit step failed), `git commit --no-edit` concludes it; then manually `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` the agent worktree
openapi.json formatting drift from `nest build` side-effects accumulates in the main tree and must be restored with `git checkout --` before worktree merges to avoid spurious conflicts
Phase 43 gap closure required 4 additional plans (43-05 through 43-08) spawned from verifier findings — the gap-closure wave loop is a normal part of the execute-phase pipeline, not a failure mode

friction: 1Password SSH signing failures mid-session required user to restart the desktop app; no workaround exists except waiting — any batch of commits is blocked until recovery
gsd commit helper false negatives (`committed: false` when commit actually landed) caused unnecessary retry confusion and wasted investigation time on multiple occasions
Worktree cleanup helper is not idempotent — partial failures require manually constructing a reduced manifest with only un-merged entries; the helper aborts the entire run on the first blocked entry
Session quota interruptions ('You've hit your session limit') twice disrupted active executor wave dispatching, requiring re-inspection of worktree states to determine what needed to be re-dispatched
planner agent socket error after writing plans 01-03 for phase 42 required filesystem fallback verification and spawning a continuation planner agent for plans 04-08
zsh multi-glob rm (`rm -rf node_modules apps/*/node_modules`) aborts entirely if any glob has no matches — requires single explicit paths
cleanup-wave cwd bug: running the helper from inside an agent worktree causes false base_mismatch errors because it resolves repoRoot from cwd
42-05 merge left MERGE_HEAD after auto-resolving all conflicts but failing the commit step — required manual `git commit --no-edit` then worktree cleanup
No .prettierignore caused prettier to corrupt planning doc markdown tables (broke regex pipe characters into spurious table columns), only discovered after commit

User explicitly called out that the assistant presented a menu instead of answering the direct questions about unpin endpoint exposure and CID discoverability — required a full code investigation before giving a direct prose answer
Decision coverage gate D-07 failed due to mechanical grep requiring a literal `D-07:` citation string in the plan even though the decision was substantively addressed
pnpm flag forwarding inserts `--` between pnpm args and jest args, causing `--testPathPattern` to be misinterpreted as a positional regex — cost a debug cycle to identify
